$comment: RFC-0052. A dashboard request to a spec whose every number is defined and whose every query has been reviewed. The spec comes first so only the queries behind charts that survive the cut list are reviewed; the metric's owner signs last, because only they can say a definition is what the business means.
name: measure
description: Take a dashboard request to a spec a BI developer can build on numbers people can defend: the decision it serves and one chart per question, every metric defined, the SQL behind each metric reviewed for the bugs that quietly inflate a figure, and the metric owner's sign-off on each definition before anything is built. Use when the user says "we need a dashboard for…", "run the measure loop", "make sure these numbers are right before the BI team builds it", or two teams disagree about a number that is about to go on a dashboard.

stages.intent: Pin the audience and the decision, keep only the charts that serve it, and name the defined metric behind each, flagging any metric nobody has defined.
Review the query behind every metric that survived the cut list, correctness before performance, with corrected SQL and the queries that prove the fix.
Each metric's owner confirms its definition and the number its reviewed query now produces. The critique informs that decision; it does not make it.
